newsitem.title: CHINA: HK&Shanghai Hotels down on dull outlook.
newsitem.headline: HK&Shanghai Hotels down on dull outlook.

text.p: Shares of Hong Kong & Shanghai Hotels Ltd fell further on Friday on long liquidation after the hotelier reported dull interim earnings and due to anticipation of an unexciting outlook for the industry, brokers said.
The shares fell HK$0.55 or 4.82 percent to HK$10.85 in late morning, after easing HK$0.25 or 2.15 percent on Thursday. Volume was 3.36 million shares worth HK$36.72 million.

"Investors are switching away from the hotel sector on expectation of a limited upside in view of a dull earnings outlook for the hotel sector," said Ben Kwong, research director of Dharmala Securities.
"Anticipation of more hotel room supply in future which can soften room rate due to competition also triggered selling," Kwong said.
Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels had on Thursday posted an eight percent rise in interim profit to HK$412 million for the six months to June 30.
The hotelier said it would see a slowdown in earnings growth in second half 1997 due to weak demand in the remaining summer months and renovation work at the Kowloon Hotel.
